title: 18. What's That Smell?
reviewMethod: English read-aloud translation compared with every original Korean page

pages.text: Dubu had played happily in the yard all day, racing after a ball and splashing through muddy puddles. Woof, woof! This is the best fun! Dubu was sweaty and grubby but still very happy.

At night, Mom said, Dubu, let's wash up and go to bed! But Dubu's eyes were closing, and that tired body felt heavy. Skipping one wash won't matter, will it? Still grubby, Dubu slipped under the covers.
The next morning, Dubu got out of bed and went straight to the Rainbow Class. Yesterday's dirt and sweat were still there. Nobody will notice! Dubu opened the classroom door bravely.
But as soon as Dubu sat down, Toto began to sniff. Huh? What's that smell? Kongi held their nose, too. Something smells funny! The friends looked around for the smell.
Sniff, sniff. They followed the smell and found Dubu! Nearby, the friends held their noses. At last, Dubu realized. Is that smell coming from me? Dubu's face turned red, and those ears drooped.
Embarrassed, Dubu crept into a corner, tucked that tail between both legs, and looked down. This happened because I didn't wash. What can I do? Dubu almost cried.
Then Bori came over gently and held out a hand, without any teasing. It's okay, Dubu. Nobody will tease you. Let's wash up together today! Bori's warm words helped Dubu feel better.
Dubu held Bori's hand and went to the sink. Rub, rub, with soap. Fluffy bubbles rose! They washed away the dirt and sweat. Wow! I feel so fresh! Dubu's white fur shone clean again.
When clean Dubu returned, the friends sniffed again. Wow, you smell lovely and fresh now! Toto and Kongi smiled and held Dubu's hands. Dubu, let's play together! Dubu wagged that tail happily.

That night, Dubu washed before bed without being told. Washing every day feels so fresh and nice! Dubu smiled under the covers. After a day of play, washing up helps us feel comfortable and ready for more fun with friends.
